findings: Yongxiao Lin, 'Short mollifiers of the Riemann zeta-function', arXiv:2508.11108 (Aug 2025): calculus of variations on LINEAR COMBINATIONS OF ZETA-DERIVATIVES in Levinson's method; positive proportion of on-line zeros regardless of how short the mollifier is; MORE THAN DOUBLES the proportions for modular L-functions (vs Bernard and Kuehn-Robles-Zeindler) with the SAME arithmetic inputs. Interpretation: the derivative-combination (Q-polynomial) side is optimizable at fixed short length - it does NOT move the LENGTH-theta frontier. Quoted: 'optimizing the linear combinations ... has a more pronounced effect than refining the mollifier when it is short'. The length barrier (off-diagonal at theta > 1/2, moment at theta > 4/7) is untouched. ALSO: the construction gives 'non-trivial smooth approximations of Siegel's f-function in the Riemann-Siegel formula'.
